risks.risk: Seller's claimed brand/model (Yamaha DGX-200) cannot be confirmed, and this model carries a specific, much higher market value than a generic unbranded keyboard.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the brand logo and model label, usually printed above the keys or on the back/underside of the unit.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a generic unbranded portable keyboard, not as a Yamaha DGX-200

risks.risk: Keyboard may not power on or keys/buttons may not function.
risks.proof: A photo or short video of the unit powered on, screen lit, and a key being pressed with sound.

risks.risk: No power adapter shown; keyboard may be unusable without one, and adapters for specific models can be hard to source.
risks.proof: Photo of the power adapter/cable included with the sale.

risks.risk: Physical condition of keys, screen, and speaker (scratches, cracked keys, dead pixels, blown speaker) cannot be fully assessed from one distant photo.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the full key range, screen display, and speaker grille from multiple angles.
risks.if_unproven: priced at worst-case visible condition (assume cosmetic and functional wear)

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the brand logo and model number plate on the keyboard.
Video of the keyboard powering on, screen displaying, and keys producing sound.
Photo of the power adapter included with the sale.
Close-up photos of the key range and screen for cosmetic condition.
response.reason: The seller's claimed brand and model (Yamaha DGX-200) would set the price, but no brand or model text is legible in the single photo provided, so even a worst-case price cannot be anchored without confirming whether this is the claimed model or a generic keyboard.
